Knowing what makes each AI agent special is part of knowing how to use them

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

ChatGPT and Claude are two of the biggest names in AI, and both have become significantly more capable within the last few months. Whether you need help writing an email, researching a topic, creating an app or managing your workload, both chatbots can handle far more than simple questions and answers. But despite their similarities, OpenAI and Anthropic have taken different approaches to building their AI assistants.

ChatGPT has evolved into an all-purpose assistant with tools for everything from image generation and voice conversations to coding and research. Claude has become hyper-focused on writing, programming and helping users complete more complicated tasks through its growing collection of productivity tools.Now that Anthropic has gone public, people are beginning to wonder what is so special about the company's AI known as Claude.

I've spent plenty of time testing both, and while there's considerable overlap between what they can do, there are some differences worth understanding before deciding which one deserves your time and money.

Here are five of the biggest differences between Claude and ChatGPT.

Claude has developed a reputation for producing natural-sounding text that is especially true for longer pieces. It's also good at following detailed writing instructions and maintaining a consistent tone and style across multiple rounds of editing.

And while ChatGPT is no slouch when it comes to writing, either, it has the advantage of flexibility. You can ask it to rewrite something in five different tones, brainstorm headline ideas or transform a complicated explanation into something a beginner can understand.So, while Claude may be the better starting point for someone writing a novel or polishing a lengthy document, ChatGPT is especially useful when experimenting with different approaches.

Of course, writing quality is subjective. The results also depend on which model you're using and how clearly you explain what you want.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

One of ChatGPT's biggest advantages is how many different types of tasks it can handle within the same experience.

Alongside traditional text conversations, ChatGPT supports image generation and editing. You can describe a picture you want to create, upload an existing image to change its appearance or use the chatbot to develop visual concepts.

ChatGPT also offers voice conversations, so users can speak naturally with the assistant instead of typing everything into a chat window.

Claude has expanded its creative capabilities, too, particularly through Artifacts, which lets users create interactive content, visualizations and applications.

However, Claude's creative tools are more focused on building useful digital experiences than generating standalone images.

For anyone who regularly switches between writing, visual creation and spoken conversations, ChatGPT offers a more versatile experience.

Coding or "vibe coding" has become one of the biggest battlegrounds between Anthropic and OpenAI.

Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent, designed to work directly with codebases, understand existing projects, make changes and help developers solve complicated programming problems.

It has become particularly popular with developers who want an AI assistant that can work inside their existing development environment.

OpenAI's answer is Codex, which can also navigate repositories, write code, fix bugs and handle development tasks.

Both tools go well beyond generating snippets of code in a chatbot. They can take on larger assignments and work through multiple steps of a project.

The biggest difference is often how developers prefer to work. Claude Code has strong roots in terminal-based development, while Codex offers workflows across different development environments and agent-based tasks.

For casual users who occasionally need help building a website or debugging a script, either chatbot can be useful. Developers working on larger projects may find that their preferred coding agent becomes the deciding factor. Personally, I tend to hit my usage limits and blast through tokens faster with Claude Code,

One of the most interesting changes to Claude is Anthropic's growing focus on turning the chatbot into a coworker.

With Cowork, Claude can take on more complicated assignments involving files, documents and connected tools. Rather than walking through every step in a conversation, users can describe the outcome they want and let Claude work through the assignment.

For example, someone could ask Claude to organize project materials, work through a collection of documents or prepare files for a presentation.

ChatGPT is moving in a similar direction with its own agent capabilities, including ChatGPT Work and Codex.

The difference is how these experiences are organized and presented to users. Anthropic has emphasized the idea of Claude as a digital coworker that can take responsibility for larger assignments. OpenAI has built a broader ecosystem that includes conversational assistance, research, creative tools and specialized agents.

Neither approach is inherently better, but if you're looking for an AI assistant to do more than answer questions, knowing the difference is important.

Price is another consideration, particularly if you're not sure how often you'll use an AI chatbot.

Both companies offer free access, although usage limits and available features vary.

ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro each cost $20 per month in the United States. ChatGPT also offers a lower-priced Go subscription for $8 per month, giving users another option between the free and Plus tiers.

Claude offers annual billing for Pro, which can reduce the effective monthly cost for users willing to commit to a full year.

Of course, usage limits, access to more powerful models and included tools can make one subscription more valuable than another. For example, if you think you're going to be creating more images and want that type of creativity from a model, than you'll want to go with ChatGPT. At the same time, if you're a casual user looking for an affordable upgrade, ChatGPT offers more flexibility in its pricing. But, if you rely heavily on Claude's writing and coding capabilities, Pro may be worth the investment.

Here's some good news: you don't have to choose between one or the other. Because ChatGPT offers so much for free, it might be worth sticking with it. But, if you find yourself going through tokens much faster with Claude, you might want to consider bumping up your subscription to a paid tier. I use both agents for different things, which brings me to another point. The bigger question is what you want your AI assistant to do.

Claude is particularly appealing for people who spend their days writing, coding or working through complicated projects. Its emphasis on natural language and increasingly capable agent tools makes it a strong choice for serious productivity work.

ChatGPT offers a broader experience. Between image generation, voice conversations, research, coding and its growing collection of productivity features, it's designed to serve as an assistant for almost anything.

If you want one AI chatbot that can handle the widest variety of everyday tasks, start with ChatGPT. If your priorities are writing, coding and managing complex workflows, Claude deserves a serious look. And since both offer free versions, the easiest way to decide is to give them the same five prompts and see which one delivers the results you actually prefer.

#3528. Forget 'Landman,' Billy Bob Thornton's Netflix Sports Drama Is a Masterpiece

Sports can be a difficult thing to capture on film. The raw passion of the crowd, the elation or despair of the result, and the personal histories we have with our teams are rarely dramatized in a way that is satisfying for those who get it. But in 2004, Friday Night Lights captured that feeling. The story of a high school football team fighting off-field struggles on its way to glory was a box office hit, inspiring a long-running TV spin-off. The reason for this longevity is a movie that combines an authentic performance from Billy Bob Thornton, excellent direction from director Peter Berg, and a script that understands just what it means to love America’s Game.

Welcome to Permian High School, an institution in Odessa, Texas, known across the community for one thing – its football team, the Permian Panthers. The coach, Gary Gaines (Thornton), is tasked with taking the team to the state championship, with elite running back James "Boobie" Miles (Derek Luke) their key to victory. However, a mix-up during a low-stakes game sees Miles get injured, throwing the season into jeopardy and piling pressure on Gaines. Off the field, the teenage athletes cope with personal problems, family issues, and the kind of pressure normally reserved for pro players. It’s up to Gaines to pull them together through the adversity, and learn how to win as a team again.

The movie is based on the real-life Permian Panthers during their 1988 season, and the real Miles himself makes a cameo as a coach. The film was a hit that led to a spin-off TV show that ran for five seasons between 2006 and 2011, which focused on another fictional town in the same state. There’s something about the original movie, however, that stands out in the crowded genre of sports films.

What happens when the hopes and dreams of a whole town rely on a group of teenage boys who haven’t begun to figure out who they are yet? That’s the question at the heart of a movie where the action ramps up when the game ends. Berg looks at the fragile nature of dreams, particularly in the world of football, where someone’s future hangs on the perfect kick, the right result, or staying injury-free. The team succeeds and fails, but the nuance of the story never gives any straightforward conclusions. The players’ personal issues are still there when they win, and losing doesn’t define who they are.

The collective passion of the parents, alumni, and staff is also a mixed blessing. On one hand, their support offers a platform for these young men to achieve their dreams. But on the other, it means Gaines dealing with numerous local figures becoming deeply invested in outcomes they cannot control, and holding the group responsible for more than just a score. It’s a uniquely American story, where an extracurricular activity can hold the hearts of an entire town, and the movie does a great job of showing the negative sides of that obsession, as well as the exhilarating highs that fuel it.

One might be tempted to portray a football coach as a hot-blooded control freak, throwing things across the locker room and giving inspirational talks to their charges. What makes Thornton’s portrayal unique is that Gaines is nothing like that stereotype, but at the same time, we’re never in doubt of the emotions lying beneath the surface. Gaines must face the responsibility of being the coach, and being held accountable for the fury of the fanbase, but at the same time protect this group of teenagers both as athletes and as people. His joy, his frustration, and his candor are delivered subtly, as he asks his team: “Can you live in that moment as best you can, with clear eyes, and love in your heart, with joy in your heart? If you can do that, gentleman, you're perfect!”

Helping him achieve that perfection is a cast of future stars, including Jay Hernandez (Suicide Squad, Magnum P.I.), Taylor Kitsch (Battleship, John Carter), and Lucas Black (the Fast and Furious franchise). These up-and-comers make their roles more than jock archetypes, instead letting the audience in on an adolescence that forces them to handle enormous pressure — in many cases without the proper guidance to deal with it.

If the ups and downs of real-life football aren’t providing enough adrenaline, Friday Night Lights provides the stakes and the personnel to make you a fan. It’s no wonder that this 2000s hit is still popular on Netflix, as the themes it covers are timeless.

I've been a fan of “Percy Jackson” for as long as I can remember. I still remember picking up the books for the first time as a kid and getting completely swept up in Rick Riordan’s world of Greek mythology, monsters and teenage demigods. It’s a franchise I’ve had a soft spot for ever since, so seeing it find a new audience through Disney’s adaptation has been a real treat. And now, somehow, we’re already heading into "Percy Jackson and the Olympians" season 3. I can’t quite believe how quickly that’s come around, but I’m certainly not complaining.

Season 3 adapts “The Titan's Curse,” the third book in Riordan’s beloved series. This time, Percy (Walker Scobell) and Grover (Aryan Simhadri) find themselves on a dangerous mission to rescue Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries), who has gone missing following an encounter with a mysterious new threat. With the fate of Olympus hanging in the balance, Percy must contend with powerful enemies and a prophecy that could change everything. It’s another big adventure for the young demigods, but one that comes with considerably higher stakes.

I’ve watched the first four episodes of season 3, and there’s plenty to get excited about. While the show still has the humor, friendship and sense of adventure that made me fall in love with the books in the first place, this latest chapter feels noticeably more mature. It’s an encouraging step forward for the Disney+ series, and one that makes me even more invested in seeing where these characters go next. Here’s what I thought of the first four episodes.

I’m Alix, a lifelong horror nerd who loves watching, reviewing and writing about the latest movies and TV shows. When I’m not working through my ever-growing horror watchlist, I’m covering the biggest releases across streaming and film, including "VisionQuest" on Disney+, "The Institute" season 2 on MGM+, and "Guarding Stars" on Netflix.

Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” wastes little time setting a darker, more action-packed tone. It opens with Thalia Grace (Tamara Smart) hunting for Luke (Charlie Bushnell) in a parking garage, where she finds herself battling a dangerous monster. Percy soon crashes into the fight. Thalia isn’t particularly thrilled about needing his help, which establishes some immediate friction between the two demigods. The opening also introduces the season’s central mission, with Annabeth explaining that she needs Thalia’s help to rescue two young demigods, siblings Nico (Levi Chrisopulos) and Bianca di Angelo (Olive Abercrombie).

Book readers will understand the significance of these characters straight away, while show-only viewers will get a better idea as the season unfolds. Thankfully, the first episode doesn't take long to get the main story moving, either, as Annabeth is abducted, triggering Percy’s fatal flaw: his unwavering loyalty. He’s determined to get her back, no matter how dangerous the quest becomes. That sense of danger carries through the first four episodes, and I think it’s one of the season’s biggest improvements.

With the group getting older and the looming threat of war becoming increasingly difficult to ignore, the show feels noticeably more mature in its storytelling. Percy and his friends are exposed to greater dangers, and there’s a stronger sense that their actions could have serious consequences. It’s also great to see the series developing Percy’s abilities, particularly his control over water. His powers have felt somewhat underexplored in previous seasons, so watching him become more confident and capable with them is a welcome change. He’s clearly getting stronger, and I hope the remaining episodes continue to build on that.

Of course, you can't talk about “Percy Jackson” without mentioning Percabeth, and I know plenty of fans are just as invested in Percy and Annabeth’s developing relationship as they are in the Greek mythology. Thankfully, season 3 gives us a little more to enjoy on that front. It’s still very much a slow burn, with neither quite ready to acknowledge that their feelings might be more than friendship, but there’s a growing awareness that something special is there. The dance scene in episode 1 is a particularly lovely example of this. I suspect season 3 will give Percabeth fans plenty to get excited about.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Based on the first four episodes, season 3 is probably the strongest “Percy Jackson” season yet. I particularly appreciate is how much more attention is given to the emotional baggage these teenagers carry as the children of some incredibly powerful figures, many of whom seem largely uninterested in their own kids’ lives. including Thalia’s complicated relationship with Zeus. We get more of an insight into how these circumstances fuel their trauma and motives.

It gives the series a little more emotional depth without losing sight of the fun. The visual effects are also stronger, with the action sequences feeling grander and more cinematic than before. There’s a real sense that the show is becoming more ambitious with each season, and these early episodes have me excited to see what’s next. If the remaining episodes maintain this momentum, “Percy Jackson” could reach a whole new level, and I can only hope Disney+ has more seasons covering the rest of the books in store.

The first two episodes of "Percy Jackson" season 3 is streaming on Disney+, with the final six episodes releasing in pairs every Friday through December 11, 2026.

#3524. Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

#3523. Russell Brand Couldn't Remember Katy Perry Wedding Date During Sex Assault Case

Russell Brand's sexual history remains under the microscope ... and newly unsealed court documents include some of his jaw-dropping testimony about Katy Perry, his genitals, and an alleged assault on a movie set.

According to court documents, obtained by TMZ, Brand was questioned about his marriage to Katy during a deposition tied to a lawsuit accusing him of sexually assaulting a female extra on the set of his 2011 movie "Arthur."

As Daily Mail first reported, Brand said he couldn't recall exactly when he married Katy, suggesting the information could be found online ... but he insisted during his deposition that he'd been completely faithful to her, claiming he'd redirected his sex addiction into their relationship.

The documents also detail allegations from a woman identified as Jane Doe ... who claims Brand exposed himself to her on set in July 2010 before cornering her in a bathroom and repeatedly demanding she "kiss his willy."

She alleges he then pushed her head down and forced his penis into her mouth for 5 to 8 seconds before she escaped.

Brand denied the allegations but acknowledged he couldn't completely rule out having exposed himself to someone without their explicit consent. He also insisted that, while he often used the term "willy" in an overtly nonsexual way, he would never use it for an actual sexual request.

A New York judge recently rejected Warner Bros. and other production companies' attempt to dismiss negligence claims in the lawsuit.

As TMZ previously reported ... Brand was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in a separate UK criminal case and sentenced to 10 years and 6 months in prison. He released a message through his wife from behind bars, saying he was "not guilty."

Casio’s 1990s-inspired digital watch is more than meets the eye

Looking for a genuinely cool tech gadget for less than $25? I’ve got just the one. The Casio WSB1000-1AV is a tough-built digital watch beaming with 1990s charm, but also a surprising smattering of modern tech niceties. Best of all, it’s 65% off for Black Friday

Need an office Secret Santa/gift exchange option that won’t break the bank? Not sure what to get for your “cool” Gen Z cousin or technologically challenged parents? The answer is this deeply discounted $22 Casio watch, which, on pretty much any other day, would cost you $64. Here are five reasons why.

Marked down from $64 to just $22, this retro-1990s Casio digital watch features an onboard step counter and Bluetooth antenna for automatic time adjustments.

Hidden behind the screen of this seemingly ordinary digital watch is a Bluetooth antenna. Why would a dumb watch need Bluetooth? To pair it with your smartphone, of course. Once paired, the Casio WSB1000 automatically corrects the time based on your smartphone’s clock.

This means there’s no need to fuss with resetting the time when traveling across time zones. The bare-bones smartphone app can also be used to set or cancel an alarm on the watch, a timer, a stopwatch, and other basic functions.

Lastly, the onboard Bluetooth plays a key role in this next feature.

You’ll notice that the Casio WSB1000 has the words “Step Tracker” printed above the LCD. This refers to this little watch’s automatic step-counting feature. Who needs the best Apple Watch or the latest Fitbit?

Like an actual smartwatch or fitness tracker, users can set daily step-count targets. The WSB1000 not only tracks your total and displays it on the watch’s LCD, but it also shows a dynamic graphic of your progress toward that day’s goal.

Bluetooth, meanwhile, is used to ping that step-count data back to your smartphone.

With onboard Bluetooth and automatic step-count tracking, battery life must be pretty short? Surprisingly, no. Casio says that the common drugstore CR2016 battery in the watch should keep it powered for approximately two years.

Afterwards, a battery swap should be a relatively painless, affordable process, done either at home (if you're savvy) or at your local jewelry store.

While the Casio WSB1000 isn’t quite as durable as watches in the brand’s legendary G-Shock range, this digital wonder is rated for 100 meters of water resistance, the same as the latest Apple Watch Ultra 4. It also boasts a shock-resistant (though not shockproof), lightweight resin case.

Ultimately, for less than $25, you're not just getting a Bluetooth-capable digital watch with step counting; you're getting the Casio WSB1000, a 90s timepiece with a design that's Tom Cruise-running-atop-a-moving-train-cool; it's Keanu Reeves-stopping-a-speeding-bus-badass... etc.

And even if your intended recipient overlooks the step tracking and tosses this watch in a drawer for occasional use, when they do eventually pull it out and pop it on, you can be sure the time and date will be spot-on thanks to the Bluetooth connection.

#3521. You Can Get One of These Pocket E-Readers for As Little As $55 Before Black Friday

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

#3519. Jonathan Rinderknecht Convicted of Starting 2025 Palisades Fire

Jonathan Rinderknecht has been convicted of starting the devastating 2025 fire in the Pacific Palisades.

A jury found Rinderknecht guilty Friday during his retrial ... about 5 months after his first one ended in a mistrial.

He's been convicted on two federal charges -- one count of destruction of property by means of fire, and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

As you know, prosecutors claimed Rinderknecht set a brush fire January 1, 2025. And even though firefighters contained the initial blaze, prosecutors say it was still smoldering for days before eventually bursting into what became the Palisades fire.

Ahead of his conviction, Rinderknecht's defense had been trying to introduce new testimony from a retired Cal Fire investigator who was pointing fingers at NBA star Chris Bosh's house.

The investigator claimed to have evidence that indicated a firework was possibly set off at Bosh's home ... suggesting it could've started the blaze instead of Rinderknecht's brush fire.

But the court was unfazed by the theory ... and Rinderknecht's sentencing is set for March 17.

#3517. Apple now selling iPhone Duo replacement parts and tools

Following last month’s launch of the iPhone Duo, which also saw the release of Apple’s official repair manuals for the device, Apple today began selling replacement parts and tools through its Self Service Repair Store. Here are the details.

Since 2022, Apple has offered its Self Service Repair program, allowing users in eligible regions to purchase replacement parts and buy or rent the tools needed to perform their own repairs on supported devices.

Just a few weeks ago, Apple began offering replacement parts and tools for several recently released devices, including the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, the latest Mac Studio, and the Mac mini.

#3515. How to hide the new macOS 27.3 menu bar indicator

macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override. Apple describes itas a transparency indicator that appears when one app is controlling another.

If you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar. Prefer to hide it? There’s a Terminal workaround.

I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.

Open Terminal and run these two commands:

sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domainsudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false

Enter your Mac administrator password when prompted, then restart your Mac.

The command disables the internal AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR feature flag. It doesn’t remove apps from your permissions list, although you’ll no longer see this activity indicator.

To restore Apple’s default behavior, run:

sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR

Restart your Mac again to apply the reversal. This removes only the indicator override, preserving any other flags you may have configured.

This is an undocumented workaround tested on the current beta, so Apple could change or remove it in a future update.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 maintains the fast, versatile ride the line is known for while adding a little more comfort, making it a successful if minor update on the Endorphin Speed 5. It’s one of the best fast trainers available and if you’ve loved past models, the Speed 6 is unlikely to disappoint, but there are some fantastic alternatives to consider too.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed has been one of the most influential running shoes of recent years, setting the template for fast training sneakers that uses some of the materials and tech from top carbon plate racers.

With the line proving so successful, Saucony has been reluctant to change much about the shoe over the five generations to date, and even though the Endorphin Speed 6 is the biggest update yet thanks to a new midsole foam, it mostly retains the same ride feel as past models.

I’ve reviewed every model of the Endorphin Speed and I’ve always been a big fan. While that’s still true with the Speed 6, this category contains some of the best running shoes available, and there are some lighter, bouncier fast trainers I rate very highly, like the New Balance SC Rebel v1 and Dynafish Xiaonian.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 costs $180 in the U.S. and £180 in the U.K., which is a $5 price rise on the Endorphin Speed 5. It’s an expensive shoe, though not out of line with other plated trainers like the Hoka Mach X3 and New Balance SC Rebel v1.

Right now the Saucony Endorphin Speed 5 is widely reduced, dropping to $104 on Amazon in the Black Friday sales, which is a factor to consider when weighing up buying the Speed

The Endorphin Speed 6 is currently available in five colors in the women’s shoe, and four colors in the men’s, including the white and yellow design I tested.

There is a wide version of the shoe available, though I found that the standard one fit me well in my normal running shoe size, the same size I’ve used with all past models of the shoe.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Saucony has added 2mm of foam to the midsole of the Endorphin Speed 6, which has a stack height of 38mm at the heel and 30mm at the forefoot, maintaining the 8mm drop of past models.

It weighs in at 8.5oz, which is 0.5oz lighter than the Endorphin Speed 5 in my size, a welcome drop for a speed-focused shoe.

The Endorphin Speed 6 has a simple mesh upper that has a little bit of padding around the tongue and collar, but mostly focuses on being lightweight and breathable.

It’s my preferred kind of upper on any shoe, since it’s not oppressively padded on the tongue or overly stiff around the heel, and I found the fit comfortable and secure throughout all my runs.

The Endorphin Speed 6’s main changes are in the midsole, which is made from a new foam called PWRRUN PBX, which is meant to be lighter and bouncier than the PWRRUN PB that has been used on all past models of the shoe.

There’s also the higher stack and a redesigned nylon plate in the midsole, which aims to create a smoother, faster ride, with the Speedroll rocker on the shoe also contributing to this.

The changes to the midsole are noticeable on the run, though not as dramatically as I expected when looking at the spec sheet for the Speed 6.

Rubber is used sparingly on the bottom of the Speed 6 to keep the weight down, but patches cover the forefoot and heel of the shoe, and in my experience Saucony’s pelletized midsole foams are durable even when the foam is exposed on the bottom of a shoe.

Grip hasn’t always been a positive feature on the Speed line, but the Speed 6 provided me with reliable traction in wet conditions on both the road and the track during my testing.

After the very pleasant surprise of the original Endorphin Speed, which I ran over 300 miles in, I’ve found that the line has delivered a reliably similar experience with all of the models since.

There have been updates to make it more stable and comfortable, but ultimately all five versions of the Speed to date have had a smooth, fast and versatile ride feel.

This is still true of the Endorphin Speed 6 for me, and while that’s mostly a positive in that it performed well across a variety of runs in my testing, some might have hoped for a bigger change to challenge rivals like the SC Rebel v1 and cheaper, lighter options like the Adidas Adizero Evo SL and Dynafish Xiaonian.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

The rockered midsole pushes you smoothly through your footstrike, and while the midsole foam isn’t as soft and springy as some, it does give a good amount of energy return off the toes.

I also found the Speed 6 to be quite stable and comfortable for easy runs, which is not always the case with plated trainers like this. I could happily use it for pretty much any kind of run, though it’s not as fast as a true carbon plate racer, or as comfortable as a max-cushioned cruiser.

To compare it directly to the Endorphin Speed 5 I did a short run wearing both shoes, and while the Speed 6 is a little bouncier and more comfortable, especially under the forefoot, I still felt the two shoes had a similar ride feel.

The Speed 6 is still a bit firmer than most super-trainers, and not as comfortable as more cushioned shoes under the toes. Some will like this more direct ride feel, but I appreciate the extra softness and bounce of a shoe like the SC Rebel v1.

If you’re a long term fan of the Endorphin Speed line the Speed 6 will be a winner. It’s a mild improvement on the previous models with extra cushion and bounce, and delivers the versatile performance you expect from the line.

There is certainly a case for getting the Speed 5 instead in sales in my opinion, but the Speed 6 is a slightly better shoe overall and a successful update.

The Speed line has been faced with increasingly fierce competition in recent years, and I don’t think the Speed 6 does much to change the equation on this front.

If you want a lighter, bouncier fast trainer, the New Balance SC Rebel v1 would be my pick, while plate-free shoes like the Adidas Evo SL, Dyanfish Xiaonian and the new 361° Mega 3 Pro all offer fast, fun rides at a lower price.

As someone who would always have had the Endorphin Speed in my own rotation through the first few models, I’ve now moved on to shoes like this myself. Even though the Speed 6 is just as good as past models, I personally like the springier ride available in fast trainers.

iCloud+ already provided far more than just increased cloud storage, but with iOS 27.3 it’s set to be an asset for AI power users too.

#3510. This iPad Is a Lifehacker 'Gift of the Year' Award Winner, and It's $50 Off Ahead of Black Friday

If you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, you might be a bit intimidated by Apple's price tags. The iPad mini starts at $599; the base iPad Air is $749; and the entry-level iPad Pro is a whopping $1,199. Most of Apple's iPad line certainly lives up to its expensive reputation.

That's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

The iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

The iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

Apple says this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

The only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for users who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee plans to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Yes, Apple participates in Cyber Monday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy, Amazon, and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

#3507. Jensen Huang says he’s ready to rejoin Nvidia as CEO (if asked)

Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO shook up the AI market and US economy last week, but now via The Wall Street Journal Huang has spoken out publicly for the first time since stepping down, and he signals he’s ready to return as CEO if asked.

Today Robbie Whelan at The Wall Street Journal published Jensen Huang’s first public statement since departing Nvidia last week.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a short statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

To be clear, I’m also willing to step in as CEO of Nvidia if asked. I’ve owned several generations of their graphics cards, so I have plenty of experience with their products. More importantly, this is probably my best chance of finally having enough cash to afford a Mac with 32GB of RAM.

The timing is likely no coincidence, as Nvidia is set to report its quarterly earnings later today.

Even though Huang technically resigned as CEO rather than being fired, it was clear that his ouster wasn’t exactly his choice. Thus, today’s statement is the former CEO formally putting it out into the world that he’s ready to return if asked.

Since Huang stepped down, President Trump publicly called on Apple’s Tim Cook to step in as Nvidia CEO. But it’s expected that a new CEO—assuming it’s not Huang—will take much longer for the company to find and Cook is unlikely to want the job.

The futuristic cubic look is stylish, but more importantly, it's a seriously economical, space-saving design—which is the whole point of going adjustable over a traditional rack of individual weights. The weights have flat edges so you can hold them on end on your lap, and unlike a lot of adjustable models, they're compact enough that they won’t bump into each other on shoulder or chest presses.

These dumbbells also come in 70-pound and 90-pound versions. If you go with one of the smaller sets, you can also buy expansion sets later to upgrade to the larger versions. If you're not yet sold on adjustable dumbbells as a concept, this 150-pound set of traditional dumbbells is also discounted—down to $142.49 from $189.99.

#3505. Fiona the Hippo's Necropsy Results Revealed After Her Death

Fiona the Hippo's necropsy results found that no effort to save the animal would have worked after the beloved hippopotamus swallowed a knit hat.

The Cincinnati Zoo shared Friday that her necropsy showed the hat had been lodged in the middle of her small intestine for days before she died.

To put that in perspective, the piece of clothing was located about 50 feet from the end of her intestines.

Cincinnati Zoo's director of animal health, Dr. Mike Wenninger, said ... "Upper and lower GI endoscopy were unable to reach the object. The location and anatomy made laparoscopic removal impossible. No treatment aside from supportive care had any chance for success, and the necropsy confirmed that no amount of supportive care would have worked."

We reported earlier ... Fiona ate the hat last week after a child threw it into the enclosure. In a freak accident, the hat managed to hit a fan and slip past a gap to find its way into Fiona's habitat.

Unfortunately, vets who tried to remove it were unsuccessful.

#3503. These Are the Best Early Black Friday Deals on Kindles and E-Readers

Amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save big on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a new model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

If you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

If you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

If you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.)

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (currently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. #3502. VSCO launches its first native Mac photo editor with RAW support, batch editing, more

VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

Professional and amateur photographers just got a new alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the company’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the company’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing users to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:

“Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

The first thing users will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

As for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Users can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the company’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for quickly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

And speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow users to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for users looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are new organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow users to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Once users are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, users can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

VSCO Studio Pro Desktop is available today as a free download for Apple Silicon Macs, with full feature access requiring a VSCO Pro membership, starting at $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year, or a VSCO One membership. You can see it in action below:

To learn more about VSCO Studio Pro Desktop, follow this link.

#3500. Bowers & Wilkins’ High-End Headphones Are Currently on Sale for Less Than Bose and Sony Models

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

Bowers & Wilkins has long been one of our favorite brands for bookshelf speakers and headphones, but the name typically carries a high price tag. Their headphones fetch for $800, while the most high-end pair of B&W loudspeakers will set you back over $100,000.

Fortunately, not every B&W product is that expensive — right now, the brand’s Px7 S2e over-ear noise-cancelling headphones are discounted to $229. Typically $400, the headphones feature a similar design to the brand’s most high-end models and identical battery life.

Available in cloud grey, forest green, and ruby red

It’s considerably less than the latest headphones from brands like Apple, Bose, and Sony, although certain colors are already sold out. For now, you can still pick up a pair of the headphones in cloud grey, forest green, and ruby red.

While we haven’t tested the Px7 S2e model, on paper, they have a lot of the same features that we love about the Px8 S2. They have the same solid 30-hour battery life, plus noise-canceling with an ambient setting. You also get wear detection (so the headphones pause when you take them off) and a zippered carrying case.

The headphones also feature tactile buttons, rather than touch controls. There’s a slider to power the headphones on, distinct buttons for raising and lowering volume, a multifunction playback button, and a button to switch noise-canceling modes.

There are some tradeoffs with these headphones compared to the flagship model. B&W swapped the high-end leather finish for fabric, and the headphones use 40 mm bio-cellulose drivers, rather than the carbon drivers used by the Px8 S2 headphones.

The flagship model also uses Qualcomm’s AptX Lossless codec for higher resolution audio over Bluetooth, compared to the AptX Adaptive codec used by the S2e model for high (although your source device has to support the codec for the best result). That said, you still get many of the flagship model’s great features at a much (much) lower price.

If you’re looking for a higher-end pair of cans, Bowers & Wilkins’ first-gen Px8 headphones are also discounted. They feature the bells and whistles Bowers is known for, including Nappa leather earcups and aluminum details. The newer Px8 S2 features some upgrades, including a slimmer, more comfortable fit, but the Px8 are still top-tier headphones. It’s rare to find headphones made with leather and metal components at this price; for $479, they’re only slightly more expensive than other flagship headphones. Like Bowers’ other headphones, these feature up to 30 hours of battery life, which is enough for most trips and daily use.

#3497. If You Loved 'Phony,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Our relationships are foundational to our lives—our sense of safety and how we understand the world around us. When someone close to us suddenly, imperceptibly shifts, it can be unsettling, especially because you can’t be sure what’s changed or why. Those are the waters where Hulu’s Phony swims, delivering a perfectly pitched dramedy about a teenager (Sam Nivola) who emerges from a brief coma convinced that his mother (a pitch-perfect Connie Britton) has been replaced with a double. If you loved the series (and similar shows) and you’re looking for more intriguing stories about doubles and impostors close to home, you should definitely watch Goodnight Mommy.

Goodnight Mommy definitely leans into the psychological horror aspect of an impostor mother much, much harder than Phony, but it’s just a deeper dive into the show’s darker implications (and, fair warning, this movie is dark).

A woman identified only as Mother returns from having cosmetic surgery with her face totally enveloped in bandages, and her twin sons observe strange differences in her behavior that convince them she isn’t their real mother—she appears to ignore one of her sons completely, and disciplines them much more harshly than before. The boys also find clues that bolster their fears, including a photograph showing their mother posing with a woman dressed identically to her.

The boys’ attempts to force her to confess rapidly descend into a kind of madness, ultimately leading them to tie her to the bed in an effort to force her to admit she’s not their real mother. It all leads to a reveal as affecting as Phony’s ultimate explanation (albeit a lot more grim and violent). The film goes way harder than the series, but if you were totally into the premise, this is the more horrifying version you’ll want to see. The original film is German; there was a 2022 remake starring Naomi Watts, and while it's pretty good, the original is the right choice. Stream Goodnight Mommy on Kanopy or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

Looking for more impostor stories that dig into the psychological and emotional impact of suspecting someone has been replaced? Here are a few more movies that dig into the concept.

The Hole in the Ground offers an inversion: A mother who becomes convinced that her son has been replaced by an impostor. Firmly in the supernatural horror genre, the story still plays the same game with the viewer: Is Sarah (Seána Kerslake) crazy, or has her son, Chris (James Quinn Markey), been replaced by a creature living in the woods near their home? It’s got the same disturbing energy as Sarah struggles with how much her son’s changed behavior is her own psychological projection and how much is clear evidence that he’s no longer the same person—or, possibly, even the same species. Stream The Hole in the Ground on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

Taking a slightly more literary approach (it’s based on a novella by Fyodor Dostoyevsky), The Double explores what happens if you find yourself replaced by a doppelgänger. Simon (Jesse Eisenberg) is a nonentity—ignored at work, lonely, and silently longing for the girl living across the street, Hannah (Mia Wasikowska). One day, a new employee named James appears at Simon’s job—and James looks exactly like Simon. But James is assertive, confident, and charming, sending Simon into a spiral. As the two versions slide into a battle for dominance, Simon finds himself turning to increasingly deranged moves to rid himself of the new and improved version of himself. If you loved the psychological implications that Phony explores, check out The Double. Stream The Double on Kanopy, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

On one level, Denis Villeneuve’s 2013 film is about a college professor named Adam (Jake Gyllenhaal) who discovers an actor named Anthony who looks exactly like him (also played by Gyllenhaal). When he tracks his double down, their lives merge in messy ways, ending in tragedy and one of the most striking (and confusing) final shots in cinema history. On another level, Enemy is a deft trick, exploring someone’s subconscious using dream logic and misdirection. If the best part about Phony was the disorienting sense that a secret just under the surface will explain everything, Enemy is the perfect choice. Stream Enemy on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

If you’re looking for a deeper, crazier, and more terrifying story about doubles, Andrzej Żuławski’s 1981 film is a terrific choice. Inspired in part by his own feelings in the wake of a painful divorce, the story follows Mark (Sam Neil), a spy who returns to West Berlin at the height of the Cold War only to find out his wife, Anna (Isabelle Adjani), has been having an affair and wants a divorce. But Anna’s behavior becomes increasingly strange, and then Mark meets their son’s teacher, Helen, who looks just like Anna. And that’s before Anna kind of ... grows a replacement Mark from a tentacled creature kept in her bathroom (and that’s just the beginning of how weird this movie gets), resulting in two doubles. How much of the film is meant literally and how much simply represents the trauma of romantic betrayal and divorce is up to you, but Possession will definitely leave a mark. Stream Possession on Shudder, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Obsession looks at the Doppelgänger Effect from a different perspective. Cliff Robertson plays Michael Courtland, a wealthy businessman whose wife (Geneviève Bujold) and young daughter, Amy (Wanda Blackman), are kidnapped in 1959. When he follows police advice against delivering the ransom, both appear to be killed in an explosion. Courtland spends the next 16 years hating himself, until he encounters a young woman, Sandra (also Bujold), who looks almost exactly like his late wife. He works to make Sandra look as much like his wife as possible, and eventually proposes—but then Sandra is kidnapped in precisely the same way as his wife and daughter sixteen years before. This all leads to a head-spinning series of reveals and a twist that echoes the Hitchcock classic Vertigo. Rent Obsession on Prime Video.

#3494. This Apple Watch Is a Lifehacker 'Gift of the Year' Award Winner, and It's $50 Off Ahead of Black Friday

Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

#3493. The Google Wallet app is now available on iOS

Google Wallet is now available on iOS to “organize purchases, tickets, boarding passes, and more in one easy place” in the US.

The Google Wallet app on iPhone does not offer tap-to-pay functionality due to platform restrictions. Instead, Google touts three intended use cases:

App navigation is handled by a floating pill (in Liquid Glass) with two tabs. The homepage starts with a carousel of recent purchases slated for delivery, followed by boarding passes, and finally a grid of loyalty cards.

The next tab shows a list of recent transactions associated with Google. The Wallet app will display purchase emails and summarize them. You also get a list of Passes, which you can pin/unpin from the homepage, and payment methods saved to your Google Account.

The ‘plus’ FAB (floating action button) lets you add loyalty, gift, and payment cards (for use in Chrome). There’s a convenient “Everything else” camera scanner that can be used to digitize anything else.

The other main reason Google Wallet now exists on iOS is that the company wants the app to be a “secure hub for managing agentic purchases across Google.”
