#3490. Why Black Friday and Cyber Monday Are Bad Days to Impulse Buy Electronics

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Some Cyber Monday deals are still live, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Follow our live blog to stay up-to-date on the best sales we find.

Browse our editors’ picks for a curated list of our favorite sales on laptops, fitness tech, appliances, and more.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

When you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be said for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before new models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The issue isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

The key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

If you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

#3489. OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT and Codex with new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models

OpenAI kicked off the GPT-6 generation with Astra in September, then upgraded Sol to GPT-6.1 a few weeks later at DevDay.

Today, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are coming to ChatGPT Work and Codex together. OpenAI says both can finish demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done before hitting your usage limit.

Astra is still the model OpenAI recommends for your hardest projects.

Say you have a screenshot of a slide and want the rest of your presentation to look like it. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra can use that screenshot as a template and match the layout, colors, and even the font size.

On the Codex side, OpenAI says Astra is better at making and testing changes in an existing project.

“Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision,” OpenAI says.

Sol is the more affordable model for everyday coding and writing, and it gets surprisingly close to Astra on one coding test.

Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 measures whether changes to real codebases are good enough for maintainers to merge.

With both models at maximum reasoning effort, OpenAI says Sol came within half a point of Astra at about one-fifth the cost.

Some of you have been asking very politely. Some of you have just been asking.GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available.Super efficient and built to perform where it counts—the real world.https://t.co/qr2iP0GpfX pic.twitter.com/jLCyVIws2Y

Both models are available starting today in ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu.

The $200/month Pro plan also gets Ultrafast mode for the first time with Sol. The $500/month Pro plan gets Ultrafast on both models, as do eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces once an admin enables it.

How fast is Ultrafast? OpenAI says it can generate tokens at up to 4.5 times the standard rate on either model, although it uses more of your allowance. You can switch speeds from the model picker.

Developers can use both models through the API today as well. Astra’s standard input and output prices are 20% lower than with GPT-6 Astra, while Sol keeps its GPT-6.1 pricing.

Quite frankly, the Hyundai Ioniq 9 gets a bad rap for the way it looks. In fact, I said in my 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 review that the design is an “odd mashup featuring a curvy front bumper with an even stranger-looking arched rear.” It’s one of the last SUVs I’d expect to win any beauty awards.

That’s why I drove the Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design for the second time this year — just to convince myself that there are better 3-row midsize SUVs out there. I’ve spent more time testing 3-row SUVs than any other vehicle type this year, with models like the Kia Telluride, Volvo XC90, Volkswagen Atlas, and Lucid Gravity getting my seal of approval.

But after another week behind the wheel, I can tell you firsthand that judging the Ioniq 9 by its cover is a mistake. Here’s what I realized.

As with most vehicles, fuel economy and efficiency tend to dwindle over time — which is why I’m shocked that the Ioniq 9 is an exception. I was already impressed by the 3 mi/kWh average I got when I drove it last year, yet my second run delivered even better results.

Across 130.5 miles of mixed driving, my second go-around with the Ioniq 9 yielded an impressive 3.3 mi/kWh. What surprised me even more was the substantial improvement in city driving, where I recorded a peak tally of 4.5 mi/kWh — up from my previous best of 3.8 mi/kWh.

Considering it’s marketed as a three-row family hauler, it’s remarkable that the Ioniq 9 can post numbers like this. That extra efficiency is critical, too: while this trim carries an EPA-estimated range of 311 miles, averaging 3.3 mi/kWh puts its real-world range closer to 363 miles.

I’ll admit I was harsh on the Hyundai Ioniq 9’s styling the first time around. While it certainly takes cues from the subcompact Hyundai Kona, I argued that it was an odd mashup that was confused about what aesthetic it was trying to go after.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

After spending another week with it, though, its unconventional look slowly grew on me — even if that appreciation is mostly isolated to the front of the EV. That’s due to Hyundai’s signature Parametric Pixel LED light bar, which stretches across the nose like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Those individual blocks give it a retro look that becomes even more dazzling from dusk into the night. In a sea of generic crossovers, this one certainly commands road presence.

That said, I still haven’t come to terms with the back half of this electric SUV. That tapered, upright rear end remains the hardest pill to swallow, giving it the look of a boat tail. Despite this, I now appreciate that the shape is doing the heavy lifting to make it aerodynamic — and subsequently boosting its efficiency.

Whether I’m making a quick stop at the local grocery store or on my 30+ mile commute to work, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 doesn’t skimp on the comforts. Step inside, and it’s clear Hyundai prioritized first-class comfort for the people riding up front and in the middle.

For example, the plush H-Tex seats strike a great balance of softness and support — which, for the driver, includes extra pampering courtesy of Hyundai’s Ergo Motion seat. When activated, it slowly adjusts the firmness of the cushion, sort of like getting a mini massage while driving, all to deter fatigue on longer hauls.

Still, the real VIP treatment belongs to the second-row captain’s chairs. With both heating and ventilation, plus power-reclining backrests and extendable footrests, they turn the middle row into a rolling lounge. However, the third row leaves more to be desired. Although I still appreciate having the extra seating capacity in a pinch, the legroom back there is practically nonexistent for adults — so I’d much rather keep that rear bench folded flat to make way for more trunk space.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design comes loaded with just about every luxury and tech perk anyone could ask for — and rightfully so.

​I still absolutely love Hyundai's adaptive cruise control, which makes long drives bearable and includes a dedicated lane-centering button on the steering wheel that also happens to work on local roads. Adding to that is a crisp Head-Up Display that projects my speed and navigation right onto the windshield.

​Changing lanes is effortless thanks to the Blind-Spot View Monitor (which streams a live camera feed straight into the digital gauge cluster) and a digital rearview mirror that offers a wider field of view than a conventional glass mirror.

​Back-seat passengers get plenty of love, too, with built-in rear side-window sunshades, a massive panoramic sunroof, and dazzling customizable ambient lighting that sets an upscale mood after dark.

​There’s also practical utility in the form of a handy 120V outlet accessible right in the trunk, letting me power laptops, tailgating gear, or small appliances straight off the SUV’s battery.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design is easily one of the most expensive vehicles in Hyundai’s entire lineup — and that price tag has long made me a skeptic.

​Yet spending a second week behind the wheel proved that judging it at face value is a mistake. Between its even better real-world efficiency, spacious cabin suited for families, and a laundry list of thoughtful luxury features, the Ioniq 9 delivers where it counts most: a family hauler that's rich in utility and backed by an efficient drive.

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

Plenty of content has been migrating to streaming services for years now, but some of the most popular programming is still only available on traditional TV. From sports like NFL, college football, and NBA games to awards shows, some content is still most easily accessible via a traditional channel guide.

Luckily, if you don’t want a traditional cable or satellite package, there are now a handful of standout live TV streaming services that beat those dying cable boxes with better pricing, more streamlined packages, and viewing flexibility.

One of those standout live TV streaming services is Fubo. The popular service offers hundreds of channels in a selection of well-priced packages. If you’re looking to ditch cable — or find a way to access channels you lost by cutting the cord — it’s a great option.

Fubo offers more than 250 channels in its top-tier subscription. These channels include network stations ABC, CBS, and FOX, plus all of the most popular cable channels and regional sports networks (in certain packages). Cable channels include standouts like ESPN, FS1, Fox News, MSNBC, HGTV, CNN, Bravo, and Hallmark Channel. The only notable absence on Fubo is TNT. See Fubo’s full channel lineup here.

Fubo plans start at $64.99 a month, and the service’s most expensive package is $98.99 a month. Similar top-tier packages from other streamers can easily surpass $100 a month, making Fubo’s pricing very competitive.

Here’s a quick breakdown of Fubo’s (English-language) package offerings:

Sports + News: Fubo’s Sports + News plan is a streamlined, affordable option that costs $64.99 a month. You get 30+ channels, including local stations (ABC, CBS, NBC, and FOX), Fox News, and sports channels like ESPN, FS1, and NFL Network.

Pro: Fubo’s Pro plan costs $88.99 a month and offers a great balance of price and channel availability. It includes local channels, regional sports networks, cable sports channels, news stations, and a huge selection of entertainment channels.

Elite: Fubo’s largest package is Elite, which offers over 250 channels and — unlike the options above — 4K UHD high-resolution streaming for certain content. It costs $98.99 a month.

Another important note: all Fubo packages offer unlimited DVR recording and streaming on up to 10 screens at a time. That’s a better deal than any other live TV streaming service, and frankly, it’s shocking that both perks are available in all packages.

Fubo is currently offering deals on all of its plans. New users can get a discount of up to $30 off their first month, depending on the plan they select. You can get $25 off your first month with the Pro plan and $30 off your first month with the Elite plan.

#3485. How to Cancel Your Amazon Prime Membership After Black Friday and Cyber Monday

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

One of Amazon’s biggest sales of the year, Black Friday and Cyber Monday, is set to start Nov. 27, but many early deals are already rolling in. To take advantage of everything the sale has to offer, you’re going to need to be a Prime Member. If you sign up for an Amazon Prime account to take advantage of the sale but decide you don’t want to pay for an ongoing membership, you’ll need to cancel your subscription before the end of your free trial.

You can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

The changing of the clocks has taken its toll on my sleep this Fall. After long evenings bathed in artificial light, I've been feeling more wired than tired at bedtime. But thanks to one surprising gadget, lately I've been more consistent with my bedtime – and that's a good thing as studies link sleep consistency with better life expectancy.

Now that I’m prioritising a consistent sleep routine, I’m also waking up less through the night. So what is this surprising gadget? A red light face mask. Were you expecting something different? Mask aside, red light is said to accentuate the production of sleep hormones.

However, sceptical that I’ve been lulling myself to sleep with nothing more than a placebo effect, I called on double-boarded sleep medicine specialist Dr. Chris Winter to ask whether the science around red lights sleep benefits checks out. Here's what he said...

Due to my job, I have a collection of gadgets to reach for when it comes to bedtime – the Ozlo Sleepbuds, Hatch Sleep Clock and the Oura Ring 5 included.

But one that's really surprised me lately is the Bob and Brad PhysioFace Light Therapy Mask, available for $169.99 (was $199.99) at Amazon.

I've been using the mask, chiefly marketed for skincare purposes, as part of my bedtime routine and it's helped me put down my phone and get to sleep on time.

As much as I love my Hatch clock, I don't love that I have to use my phone to alter settings. That's the beauty of this red light mask – it’s independent from my phone (there's no app to download) with control buttons attached to the device itself.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

That means I am actually making my bedroom a phone-free space and instead focusing on winding down for a great night's sleep.

It's hard to quantify exactly how well the red light mask is improving my sleep quality. But one thing is for sure: by the time I remove the mask, I feel sleepy and it never takes me long to dose off into a deep sleep.

According to my Garmin sleep timeline, I've reached deep sleep within half hour of dropping off, and continue to cycle through healthy sleep stages.

But what does Dr. Winter think? "It’s possible that taking a quiet break for your skincare routine is helping you unwind, particularly if it replaces scrolling or other stimulating activities.

"But feeling that you’re sleeping better doesn’t tell us whether the benefit is coming from the light itself, the routine, or something else.

"I would view it as a potentially relaxing part of your routine — not a proven sleep treatment," the board-certified neurologist cautions.

White and blue light from screens is bad news for sleep. But as the nights draw in, a lot of our evenings are powered by these types of light. This winter, I’ve been making a conscious effort to swap my overhead light for the sundown setting on my Hatch Sleep Clock. I've also been swapping doomscrolling with reading time while wearing my red light mask.

20 minutes prior to bedtime – after writing my do-to list for the following day and shutting off my phone for the night – I pop the mask on in bed and start reading a book. The 10-minute timer on the mask ensures I read for at least 10 minutes before drifting off.

The mask has three light modes with different colored lights. I've been using the BOOST mode that combines red light and near-infrared light. As well as supposedly boosting skin health, red light is associated with relaxation and there is some science associating it with improved sleep quality.

Although evidence is limited, research by Chinese scientists published in the National Library of Medicine, suggests red light influences melatonin secretion, improving sleep initiation.

Dr. Winter also referred to a 2026 review of five randomized trials that found a modest improvement in self-reported sleep quality when red light was introduced. "But the authors emphasized that the evidence was limited and imprecise," he notes.

Additionally, red light face masks, like my Bob and Brad model, are built to increase collagen production. They do this by penetrating the skin with red light, which stimulates the cells responsible for collagen synthesis. Besides improving skin elasticity, collagen can also improve sleep. A 2024 study concluded that increasing collagen at bedtime reduces sleep fragmentation.

Placebo or not, the mask has helped me prioritise a consistent bedtime routine over the past two weeks, and sleep better than I was immediately after the clock change.

I’ve been writing about sleep for over two years, and one thing I’ve learnt is that your sleep routine must be personal. A gadget or habit that works for someone else may not work for you.

If you’re struggling to sleep, you may need to try a few different methods or technologies before you hit on one that clicks. But one piece of advice sleep experts all agree on is that you need a relaxing prelude to sleep if you want to clock quality ZZZs.

A nighttime routine involves practising the same sequence of activities in the run up to your bedtime, helping prepare both your brain and body for sleep. In time, and with consistency, your body clock will come to recognise this routine as a signal to sleep, helping you drift off easily.

Dr. Winter explains: "A bedtime routine creates a predictable opportunity to step away from work, screens and other stimulating activities, rather than expecting your brain to switch off the moment your head hits the pillow. Pairing that wind-down period with a consistent sleep schedule and lower lighting helps support your body’s sleep-wake rhythm."

This routine should be "simple, enjoyable and easy to repeat" and can include activity you find relaxing, be that a dark shower, mediation, reading, stretching or simply listening to calm music.

"You don’t need an elaborate checklist or expensive equipment—the goal is to wind down, not give yourself another assignment," advises the host of the Sleep Unplugged podcast.

"Think of the routine as making room for sleep, not forcing it to happen."

One of the best sunrise alarm clocks we've tested, the Hatch Sleep Clock keeps you accountable around your sleep routine (it has integrated sleep tracking) and lulls you to sleep on time with its sundown feature and array of sleep sounds. The Hatch Sleep Clock is down to $187 in Amazon's Black Friday sale, and a subscription fee of $4.99/month gives you access to all features.

Its designed to deliver the perfect amount of essential oils in minutes to create a calm haven in your bedroom. Catch it with 17% off now, bagging you a $24/£25 saving with free delivery included.

The one for those who need total blackout to fall asleep, the SilkSound Sleep Mask is made with ultra-soft, skin-friendly silk, and laced with Bluetooth speakers to block out light and muffle unwanted sound. Our reviewer, Ruth Jones, rates the SilkSound as some of the best sleep headphones you can buy. At $34.99 now, it offers exceptional value for money, too.

#3482. Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

If you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an issue with the Duo itself.

I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for shows and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

Multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”

After a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”

The iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique new iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

What has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

#3481. The Best Music Moments and Surprise Cameos From ‘GTA VI’

The world has been waiting to play Grand Theft Auto VI, and the video game is finally here. Music, of course, is integral to all of it. There’s a soundtrack full of stars — the 34-track release, which is out today, features Travis Scott, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Arca, and more. In addition to that, there is a massive one-day festival inspired by the game, taking place in Miami on Nov. 21, with headliners Cardi B, Metro Boomin, and Justice, who also put together the game’s score.

Once you start playing, there’s even more music to discover through the game’s radio stations and celebrity DJ hosts. Here are some of the best music moments and surprise cameos from the biggest video game of the year.

The game is full of celebrity guest DJs, which Rockstar began sharing a few weeks back. There’s Cocoteo FM hosted by Bad Bunny and RaiNao, Back Country Radio hosted by Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey, and Radio La Ola with Gloria and Emilio Estefan, plus tons more. But one that may surprise people is Stockyard FM, featuring two DJs named Victoria and Harrison — better known as PinkPantheress and the Dare. Victoria and Harrison are their real names, and their radio station is dedicated to experimental, left-of-center pop, electronica, and indie sleaze.

One of the GTA VI radio stations, Radio La Ola, plays homage to Latin classics from over the decades. But one hugely surprising one is “Sopa de Caracol,” a massive but somewhat forgotten hit from the Nineties by Honduran band Banda Blanca. The inclusion made headlines in Central America, with the lead singer Pilo Tejada saying he was honored to have his voice reach new parts of the world.

Psych-rock band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard is featured on the soundtrack: They’re one of several artists on the collaboration “Flower in a Hurricane,” which also earned them their first Billboard 100 entry. But that’s not the only place you can find them: Gizz fans noticed that throughout several parts of the game, you can hear snippets of what appear to be demos from the band, woven into the score. On Reddit, diehards have been pointing these out and playing guessing games as they wonder what projects these might be from.

We’ve known that the French electronic duo Justice composed the original score for the game, but the official album won’t be out until Dec. 11. We’re getting to hear some of what they came up with the release of the game but there’s still more to come, including an anticipated collaboration with the Weeknd. The duo have since said this is the “first and last” video game they’ll ever score.

The soundtrack, which dropped on Nov. 19, is packed, featuring 34 songs by some surprising artists and stars. There’s new music from Travis Scott, the Fuerza Regida track “Suzuki,” which is charting in 15 countries, and there are also songs from Keith Richards, Kali Uchis and Helado Negro, and more. A lot of the music was inspired directly by Miami, which you can hear in new tracks from artists like JT.

Artists are getting into the game, too. Tinashe delighted fans with a hilarious livestream playing for the first time. The stream captured her making an epic getaway by flying an airplane and hysterically crashing it into the ground, then running out of ammo in a shootout. “I have no bullets!” she screams. “Holy shit, I’m going to have to beat the fuck out of them myself.” After several days of sold-out shows in the U.K., Noah Kahan stayed up late and wreaked havoc in Vice City while his wife was asleep.

The world lost D’Angelo back in 2025, but his legacy lives on in Vice City. GTA VI players discovered that an unreleased track called “Kamakazi,” as confirmed by D’Angelo collaborator DJ Dojah, is one of the songs you can hear on the radio station Worldwide FM. D’Angelo’s “Lady” also plays on the in-game Honey FM channel, which is hosted by Chilli and T-Boz of TLC.

While the creators of the game spent a ton of time adding interesting radio stations and track to the GTA VI universe, there is plenty of love for pop stars and major pop hits. Dua Lipa appears on the soundtrack, but the radio stations also feature plenty of pop girlies: There’s Chappell Roan’s “Hot To Go!,” Charli XCX’s “Good Ones,” and Addison Rae’s “Fame Is a Gun,” just to name a few, which players can blast while driving through Vice City.

#3479. AirPods Pro 3 keep getting better, here’s what’s new in iOS 27

AirPods got a variety of new features this fall in iOS 27, several of which are exclusive to AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179). Here’s everything new.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods users thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

With Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:

AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

You can change the EQ by going to your AirPods’ settings ⇾ Audio & Routing ⇾ Equalizer ⇾ Custom. From here, you can adjust the sound profile for low, mid, and high frequencies.

Custom EQ is available on AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, AirPods 5, and AirPods 4.

Apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

For more details on iOS 27’s GymKit feature for AirPods Pro 3, check out Zac’s full hands-on below.

Read more: iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

For most AirPods users, the single biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI.

Siri AI is available on compatible iPhone hardware in iOS 27, and Apple made sure to expand full support for the AI assistant to AirPods too.

AirPods are essentially becoming an AI wearable thanks to the new Siri. It will let users do a lot more than the current Siri. Here are some key features via Apple’s website:

Earlier this year when AirTag 2 launched, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of new AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

Now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.

Black Friday isn't until Nov. 27, but the early Black Friday sales are in full swing. Whether you want a full-featured fitness smartwatch or a more recovery-focused tracker, here are the discounts you can find right now, including on brands like Apple, Oura, Garmin, and more.

The Oura Ring 5 is at its lowest ever price: $299 for black and silver, $399 for all other colors. These are the lowest prices ever for these rings, which usually go for $399 and $499, respectively. The Oura Ring 5 is the smallest and most comfortable smart ring I've tried, although it's worth noting it requires a $5.99/month subscription fee.

For an even cheaper deal, the older Oura Ring 4 is $249—a full $100 off its list price of $349. If you opt for "stealth" (matte black), the price is $279; for gold, it's $286.61, down from $399. While this model has since been replaced by the Oura Ring 5, it's still an accurate and comfortable smart ring—especially if tracking your sleep is your priority.

Whoop may be one of the most expensive smart bands out there, thanks to its subscription-only model. But that price is particularly low right now, since the Peak membership that normally goes for $239 is now $199. Peak is the middle tier, and it's the one I recommend. While you can get Whoop One for $189 in this sale, the $10 you save isn't really worth it given the features you'd be missing. I also wouldn't normally recommend Whoop Life, since its ECG readings and blood pressure estimates aren't really worth the extra $100+. That said, if you do want it, the Life tier is $299 right now instead of $359.

The new Luna band is on sale for $119.20, down from a normal price of $149. The Luna band is made by Indian smartwatch company Noise, the same company behind the Luna Ring that I reviewed last year. The ring is no longer available in the U.S., but the band is. It's a Whoop-style screenless fitness tracker, potentially a worthy competitor to the Fitbit Air and other smart bands.

This is the brand-new Apple Watch model, and it's actually worth the upgrade. One of the biggest reasons is that the Series 12's new processor (called, confusingly, the S11 chip) supports some features older Apple Watches can't, and a good rule of thumb is that whenever there's a break in software compatibility, it makes sense to get the newer model. Right now, I'm seeing it for as low as $329, down from the list price of $399. (And if you're stuck deciding between an Apple Watch and a Fitbit, Beth breaks it all down in her comparison of the two watches.)

The CMF Watch 3 Pro is Nothing's latest smartwatch, and it incorporates AI features powered by ChatGPT; you can currently pick it up at a major discount. Originally $99, you can get the CMF Watch 3 Pro for $55. This is the lowest price this smartwatch has been.

If you're looking specifically for a sporty, outdoors watch, Garmin sets the standard. (You could definitely call me something of a Garmin enthusiast.) Here are the best Black Friday deals on Garmin watches that I've seen so far:

The 44mm Garmin Instinct 3 is 249.99 (down from $449.99). The 1.2-inch color AMOLED display makes the screen more readable in bright daylight conditions, and battery life is best-in-class—a must for those going off-grid.

The Garmin Fēnix 8 in titanium with a gray band is $749.99 (down from $999.99). While this is last year's model, it's a perfectly solid option if you don't specifically need the titanium case or the latest mapping engine in the latest Fenix 9 Pro.

The Garmin Forerunner 265 is $299.99 (down from $449.99). Although it isn't the latest and greatest anymore, this is still a fan favorite among Garmin users. It's a step above entry-level options, with dual-band GPS, power meter compatibility, and advanced analytics (like training status).

These aren't the only sales you'll see on fitness watches and trackers during the big shopping holiday; the following brands have announced they'll be launching more deals on Nov. 19:

Additionally, though the sale has ended, the Google Pixel Watch 5 was recently marked down by $100; I'll be keeping an eye on this device to see if that particular deal comes back once Black Friday officially arrives.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

For most people, the Apple Watch SE 3 at $199 is a good starting point, covering everyday fitness tracking, notifications, and essential health features without the higher price of the Series 12. If you want more advanced health monitoring and a more premium smartwatch experience, the Series 12 at $329 is worth considering.

Yes, Garmin is one of the best brands when it comes to rugged sports watches and fitness trackers. The Forerunner line especially, is a go-to pick for accurate and reliable GPS tracking for runners.

#3474. Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

In a new filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the company complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a new filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its new filing, Epic says Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the company of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

Apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple says decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s new CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

Under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

Given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”

According to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a new order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.

#3472. Report: iPhone set to gain market share in 2027 amid industry-wide slump

Apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a new report. Here are the details.

As detailed by AppleInsider, a new Morgan Stanley research report says Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.

The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which launched only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.

Morgan Stanley notes that this could push some purchases from late 2026 into 2027, contributing to the projected shipment growth without necessarily reflecting an increase in underlying demand.

The report also comes as Apple and the rest of the smartphone industry continue to grapple with rising memory and storage prices, though previous reports have suggested that Apple is better positioned than many of its competitors to absorb those costs.

Apple raised iPhone prices in September, after keeping them stable for much of the year while competitors had already introduced price hikes. In some cases, they raised prices more than once within a matter of months.

Back to the report, it notes that global smartphone shipments are expected to drop 5% next year, compared with a previous forecast of 3.6% growth. That said, it’s still an improvement over the estimated 13.8% decline in 2026.

When it comes to Apple and the iPhone specifically, Morgan Stanley notes that consumer interest in upgrading has remained largely unchanged year over year, with 37% of iPhone owners saying they are extremely likely to upgrade within the next 12 months. That’s compared with 41% of smartphone owners overall, a figure that dropped by 2 percentage points year over year.

As for the market’s reaction to the iPhone Duo, Morgan Stanley found that 22% of non-iPhone users surveyed expressed interest in switching to Apple’s foldable device, with that figure reaching 34% in China.

Importantly, Morgan Stanley’s survey was conducted after the iPhone Duo was announced, but before it launched, so these figures reflect consumer interest rather than actual purchasing behavior.

Apple Intelligence was another factor examined in the survey, with Morgan Stanley concluding that AI features are becoming less important in driving iPhone upgrades, while factors such as battery life and upgrade eligibility are gaining importance.

Finally, Morgan Stanley found that Apple’s customer retention rate increased three percentage points to a record 93%, while its net switching rate improved to 12%.

Huawei was the only other major smartphone brand to show a positive and improving net switching rate, while Samsung and Google remained relatively neutral, and Xiaomi, Motorola, Honor, Oppo, and Vivo recorded negative rates.

#3469. WhatsApp’s first-party chat history backup service moves ahead

Select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid plans for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp users running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

Users can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot currently be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning users switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for users running the public version without requiring another app update.

#3466. Atomically Thin Materials Significantly Shrink Qubits

MIT researchers use 2D materials for capacitors in quantum circuits in an effort to scale processors

Superconducting quantum processor and its microwave packaging.

Quantum computing is a devilishly complex technology, with many technical hurdles impacting its development. Of these challenges two critical issues stand out: miniaturization and qubit quality.

IBM has adopted the superconducting qubit road map of reaching a 1,121-qubit processor by 2023, leading to the expectation that 1,000 qubits with today’s qubit form factor is feasible. However, current approaches will require very large chips (50 millimeters on a side, or larger) at the scale of small wafers, or the use of chiplets on multichip modules. While this approach will work, the aim is to attain a better path toward scalability.

Now researchers at MIT have been able to both reduce the size of the qubits and done so in a way that reduces the interference that occurs between neighboring qubits. The MIT researchers have increased the number of superconducting qubits that can be added onto a device by a factor of 100.

“We are addressing both qubit miniaturization and quality,” said William Oliver, the director for the Center for Quantum Engineering at MIT. “Unlike conventional transistor scaling, where only the number really matters, for qubits, large numbers are not sufficient, they must also be high-performance. Sacrificing performance for qubit number is not a useful trade in quantum computing. They must go hand in hand.”

The key to this big increase in qubit density and reduction of interference comes down to the use of two-dimensional materials, in particular the 2D insulator hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The MIT researchers demonstrated that a few atomic monolayers of hBN can be stacked to form the insulator in the capacitors of a superconducting qubit.

Just like other capacitors, the capacitors in these superconducting circuits take the form of a sandwich in which an insulator material is sandwiched between two metal plates. The big difference for these capacitors is that the superconducting circuits can operate only at extremely low temperatures—less than 0.02 degrees above absolute zero (-273.15 °C).

Superconducting qubits are measured at temperatures as low as 20 millikelvin in a dilution refrigerator.Nathan Fiske/MIT

In that environment, insulating materials that are available for the job, such as PE-CVD silicon oxide or silicon nitride, have quite a few defects that are too lossy for quantum computing applications. To get around these material shortcomings, most superconducting circuits use what are called coplanar capacitors. In these capacitors, the plates are positioned laterally to one another, rather than on top of one another.

As a result, the intrinsic silicon substrate below the plates and to a smaller degree the vacuum above the plates serve as the capacitor dielectric. Intrinsic silicon is chemically pure and therefore has few defects, and the large size dilutes the electric field at the plate interfaces, all of which leads to a low-loss capacitor. The lateral size of each plate in this open-face design ends up being quite large (typically 100 by 100 micrometers) in order to achieve the required capacitance.

In an effort to move away from the large lateral configuration, the MIT researchers embarked on a search for an insulator that has very few defects and is compatible with superconducting capacitor plates.

“We chose to study hBN because it is the most widely used insulator in 2D material research due to its cleanliness and chemical inertness,” said colead author Joel Wang, a research scientist in the Engineering Quantum Systems group of the MIT Research Laboratory for Electronics.

On either side of the hBN, the MIT researchers used the 2D superconducting material, niobium diselenide. One of the trickiest aspects of fabricating the capacitors was working with the niobium diselenide, which oxidizes in seconds when exposed to air, according to Wang. This necessitates that the assembly of the capacitor occur in a glove box filled with argon gas.

While this would seemingly complicate the scaling up of the production of these capacitors, Wang doesn’t regard this as a limiting factor.

“What determines the quality factor of the capacitor are the two interfaces between the two materials,” said Wang. “Once the sandwich is made, the two interfaces are “sealed” and we don’t see any noticeable degradation over time when exposed to the atmosphere.”

This lack of degradation is because around 90 percent of the electric field is contained within the sandwich structure, so the oxidation of the outer surface of the niobium diselenide does not play a significant role anymore. This ultimately makes the capacitor footprint much smaller, and it accounts for the reduction in cross talk between the neighboring qubits.

“The main challenge for scaling up the fabrication will be the wafer-scale growth of hBN and 2D superconductors like [niobium diselenide], and how one can do wafer-scale stacking of these films,” added Wang.

Wang believes that this research has shown 2D hBN to be a good insulator candidate for superconducting qubits. He says that the groundwork the MIT team has done will serve as a road map for using other hybrid 2D materials to build superconducting circuits.

Dexter Johnson is a contributing editor at IEEE Spectrum, with a focus on nanotechnology.

#3464. iFixit tears down Apple HomeView, finds lots of glue and endless frustration

iFixit’s teardown of the new Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also showed that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%

Percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

To check out iFixit’s blog post, which features an interactive 3D CT scan of the HomeView, follow this link.

#3463. Man Found Guilty of Igniting Blaze That Became the Devastating Palisades Fire

A jury found a former Los Angeles resident guilty of starting what became the deadly Palisades Fire of January 2025, the city’s most destructive wildfire in its history.

Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Federal prosecutors accused Rinderknecht of intentionally starting the original blaze, known as the Lachman fire. While the initial fire was quickly suppressed, unbeknownst to firefighters and other authorities at the time, embers of it continued to burn underground. On Jan. 7, heavy winds reignited the fire, causing it to surface and spread. The ensuing Palisades fire was one of the most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people and decimating 23,448 acres of land and nearly 7,000 structures across the Pacific Palisades region.

“Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche in a statement. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”

“Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”

After a federal jury in June deadlocked in favor of acquittal in Rinderknecht’s first trial in June, federal prosecutors narrowed their case to charge him with the two arson-related felonies rather than the three charges in the mistrial.

Steve Haney, the man’s lawyer for both trials, told the Los Angeles Times that they planned to appeal Friday’s verdict. “We are disappointed in the verdict, but respect the jury process,” Haney told the publication. “After a lengthy deliberation, they clearly gave this case a great deal of consideration.” Trending Stories Rosalía Calls Taylor Swift a 'Master Songwriter,' Reveals Her Favorite Swift Track ‘Yes, Dear’ Star Anthony Clark's Cause of Death Revealed Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Bowen Yang Apologizes for Calling Regina Spektor Antisemitic Slur Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

The prosecution argued that Rinderknecht, who was working on New Year’s Eve as an Uber driver on Dec. 31, 2024, was angry and frustrated because he was unable to find companionship on New Year’s. According to an affidavit from an investigator for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, two of his passengers described him as “agitated and angry” that night. He allegedly drove to a Pacific Palisades trailhead, where he repeatedly listened to and watched a music video for the rap song, “Un Zder, Un Thé,” about despair, and tried calling an old friend, but was unable to connect with them.Prosecutors said that Rinderknecht started the Lachman Fire just after midnight, and that around 12:12 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2025, environmental sensing platforms indicated the Lachman fire had begun. They said that Rinderknecht called 911 several times, but didn’t get through because his iPhone was out of range. By the time he finally connected with the police, the fire had already been reported by others in the neighborhood.

During his call with police, per the affidavit, Rinderknecht also allegedly typed a question into ChatGPT: “Are you at fault if a fire is lift [sic] because of your cigarette?” ChatGPT allegedly responded “Yes.”

#3462. How AI Will Change Chip Design

Artificial intelligence’s promise and potential for the semiconductor industry

Rina Diane Caballar is a contributing editor covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment.

An array of semiconductor wafers are ready to be made into chips.

The end of Moore’s Law is looming. Engineers and designers can do only so much to miniaturize transistors and pack as many of them as possible into chips. So they’re turning to other approaches to chip design, incorporating technologies like AI into the process.

Samsung, for instance, is adding AI to its memory chips to enable processing in memory, thereby saving energy and speeding up machine learning. Speaking of speed, Google’s TPU V4 AI chip has doubled its processing power compared with that of its previous version.

But AI holds still more promise and potential for the semiconductor industry. To better understand how AI is set to revolutionize chip design, we spoke with Heather Gorr, senior product manager for MathWorks’ MATLAB platform.

How is AI currently being used to design the next generation of chips?

Heather Gorr: AI is such an important technology because it’s involved in most parts of the cycle, including the design and manufacturing process. There’s a lot of important applications here, even in the general process engineering where we want to optimize things. I think defect detection is a big one at all phases of the process, especially in manufacturing. But even thinking ahead in the design process, [AI now plays a significant role] when you’re designing the light and the sensors and all the different components. There’s a lot of anomaly detection and fault mitigation that you really want to consider.

Then, thinking about the logistical modeling that you see in any industry, there is always planned downtime that you want to mitigate; but you also end up having unplanned downtime. So, looking back at that historical data of when you’ve had those moments where maybe it took a bit longer than expected to manufacture something, you can take a look at all of that data and use AI to try to identify the proximate cause or to see something that might jump out even in the processing and design phases. We think of AI oftentimes as a predictive tool, or as a robot doing something, but a lot of times you get a lot of insight from the data through AI.

What are the benefits of using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Historically, we’ve seen a lot of physics-based modeling, which is a very intensive process. We want to do a reduced order model, where instead of solving such a computationally expensive and extensive model, we can do something a little cheaper. You could create a surrogate model, so to speak, of that physics-based model, use the data, and then do your parameter sweeps, your optimizations, your Monte Carlo simulations using the surrogate model. That takes a lot less time computationally than solving the physics-based equations directly. So, we’re seeing that benefit in many ways, including the efficiency and economy that are the results of iterating quickly on the experiments and the simulations that will really help in the design.

So it’s like having a digital twin in a sense?

Gorr: Exactly. That’s pretty much what people are doing, where you have the physical system model and the experimental data. Then, in conjunction, you have this other model that you could tweak and tune and try different parameters and experiments that let sweep through all of those different situations and come up with a better design in the end.

So, it’s going to be more efficient and, as you said, cheaper?

Gorr: Yeah, definitely. Especially in the experimentation and design phases, where you’re trying different things. That’s obviously going to yield dramatic cost savings if you’re actually manufacturing and producing [the chips]. You want to simulate, test, experiment as much as possible without making something using the actual process engineering.

We’ve talked about the benefits. How about the drawbacks?

Gorr: The [AI-based experimental models] tend to not be as accurate as physics-based models. Of course, that’s why you do many simulations and parameter sweeps. But that’s also the benefit of having that digital twin, where you can keep that in mind—it’s not going to be as accurate as that precise model that we’ve developed over the years.

Both chip design and manufacturing are system intensive; you have to consider every little part. And that can be really challenging. It’s a case where you might have models to predict something and different parts of it, but you still need to bring it all together.

One of the other things to think about too is that you need the data to build the models. You have to incorporate data from all sorts of different sensors and different sorts of teams, and so that heightens the challenge.

How can engineers use AI to better prepare and extract insights from hardware or sensor data?

Gorr: We always think about using AI to predict something or do some robot task, but you can use AI to come up with patterns and pick out things you might not have noticed before on your own. People will use AI when they have high-frequency data coming from many different sensors, and a lot of times it’s useful to explore the frequency domain and things like data synchronization or resampling. Those can be really challenging if you’re not sure where to start.

One of the things I would say is, use the tools that are available. There’s a vast community of people working on these things, and you can find lots of examples [of applications and techniques] on GitHub or MATLAB Central, where people have shared nice examples, even little apps they’ve created. I think many of us are buried in data and just not sure what to do with it, so definitely take advantage of what’s already out there in the community. You can explore and see what makes sense to you, and bring in that balance of domain knowledge and the insight you get from the tools and AI.

What should engineers and designers consider when using AI for chip design?

Gorr: Think through what problems you’re trying to solve or what insights you might hope to find, and try to be clear about that. Consider all of the different components, and document and test each of those different parts. Consider all of the people involved, and explain and hand off in a way that is sensible for the whole team.

How do you think AI will affect chip designers’ jobs?

Gorr: It’s going to free up a lot of human capital for more advanced tasks. We can use AI to reduce waste, to optimize the materials, to optimize the design, but then you still have that human involved whenever it comes to decision-making. I think it’s a great example of people and technology working hand in hand. It’s also an industry where all people involved—even on the manufacturing floor—need to have some level of understanding of what’s happening, so this is a great industry for advancing AI because of how we test things and how we think about them before we put them on the chip.

How do you envision the future of AI and chip design?

Gorr: It’s very much dependent on that human element—involving people in the process and having that interpretable model. We can do many things with the mathematical minutiae of modeling, but it comes down to how people are using it, how everybody in the process is understanding and applying it. Communication and involvement of people of all skill levels in the process are going to be really important. We’re going to see less of those superprecise predictions and more transparency of information, sharing, and that digital twin—not only using AI but also using our human knowledge and all of the work that many people have done over the years.

Rina Diane Caballar is a writer covering tech and its intersections with science, society, and the environment. An IEEE Spectrum contributing editor, she's a former software engineer based in New Zealand.

#3459. Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed

Patrick Stewart‘s cause of death has been revealed.

The beloved English actor died at age 86 on Oct. 28 in his Los Angeles home. His death was confirmed by a statement on his social media, which added that the cause was “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and lewy body dementia.”

His death certificate, obtained by People, lists cardiopulmonary arrest as his cause of death, and neurocognitive disorder with Lewy body as an underlying condition. TMZ was first to report the news.

The Emmy-winning performer known for both his good natured persona and indelible roles in popular franchises like Star Trek and X-Men, was adored by his collaborators and the public alike. Stewart’s career spanned decades with work across more than five dozen films and over 50 television appearances, from X-Men and Star Trek to Dune and American Dad. His stage roles also ran the gamut from Shakespeare’s Scottish play to Waiting for Godot to his memorable one-man version of A Christmas Carol. In 1966, he joined the Royal Shakespeare Company and he remained with the storied company until 1982. During his tenure at the Royal Shakespeare Company, Stewart featured in numerous productions, including Hamlet, King Lear, and The Taming of the Shrew. He would continue appearing onstage throughout his career, notably joining longtime friend and actor Ian McKellen for Waiting for Godot in 2009 and again in 2014.

In a wave of tributes from Hollywood following his death, William Shatner remembered Stewart, who succeeded him as captain of a Star Trek franchise. “Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor,” wrote Shatner. “From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did.”
